lede: A thank-you to Jamil bhai, who turned a personal passion into a cultural movement for Bangladesh's comic book community.
body:
Some people cover **Bangladesh's comic book culture**, and some people build it. On 4 September 2026 B-POP Tags posted a thank-you to [@akmalamgirkhanjamil](https://www.instagram.com/akmalamgirkhanjamil/), whom we called Jamil bhai, "for turning a personal passion into a cultural movement."

## Jamil's Comics and Bangladesh's comic book culture

The caption is clear about the scale of the debt: Bangladesh's pop culture and comic book community "owe a massive debt of gratitude" to his vision with [@jamilscomics](https://www.instagram.com/jamilscomics/). We closed it the only way that felt right: "Absolute legend!"

The cover is pure fan joy. Under a hand-lettered "'JAMIL BHAI'" headline, he smiles at the camera holding up a graded, slabbed Batman comic, with a crayon-blue cloud and Superman flying in from the side.

## Why one person's passion matters

Scenes like comics often start with a single obsessive who refuses to keep the hobby to themselves. They track down books, share them and give others a place to gather and talk. Over time, what began as a personal collection becomes something a whole community leans on. That's what the word "movement" in our caption is pointing to.

The post was tagged #banglacomics, #comicbookculture, #bangladeshi and #dhaka. It sits on our [pop culture hub](topic:pop-culture) next to other collector stories, including our guide to [physical media shops in Dhaka](post:physical-media-shops-dhaka-part-1) and [Dhaka's vinyl and cassette revival](post:dhaka-vinyl-cassette-revival). For a Bengali take on anime, read [Rokte Joba](post:rokte-joba-bengali-anime-ontology). More is on the [B-POP Tags home page](home:).

[See the original post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/Dc3sMdzmhdc/)
